candidates.statement: Manufacturers and distributors of drugs and the Food and Drug Adminis- tration occasionally are required to mail important information about drugs to physicians and others respon- sible for patient care. In the public in- terest, such mail should be distinctive in appearance so that it will be promptly recognized and read. The Food and Drug Administration will make such mailings in accordance with the specifications set forth in this sec- tion. Manufacturers and distributors of drugs are asked to make such mailings as prescribed by this section and not to use the distinctive envelopes for ordi- nary mail.
candidates.context: SOURCE: 40 FR 13996, Mar. 27, 1975, unless otherwise noted. Subpart A—General Provisions § 200.5 Mailing of important informa- tion about drugs. (a) Use first class mail and No. 10 white envelopes. (b) The name and address of the agen- cy or the drug manufacturer or dis- tributor is to appear in the upper left corner of the envelope.

candidates.statement: There are presently no regulations under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cos- metic Act that prevent a manufacturer of prescription drugs from sending the pharmacist data he needs on indica- tions and dosage in exercising his im- portant professional function of check- ing against possible mistakes in a pre- scription. The Food and Drug Adminis- tration believes manufacturers should be encouraged to supply such printed matter to the pharmacist for his pro- fessional information. Obviously, such printed matter should not be displayed to prospective purchasers to promote over-the-counter sale of prescription drugs.
